description: Designing, using and implementing electronic health records: what a patient record holds, clinical workflows and documentation, data models from relational schemas to openEHR archetypes, clinical decision support, usability and clinician burden, privacy, consent and access control, and implementation in low-resource clinics. Taught through case-based simulations of an outpatient clinic and district hospital, where students configure, use and critique a working record system built in the browser.
modelledOn: Shortliffe and Cimino, Biomedical Informatics: Computer Applications in Health Care and Biomedicine
Hoyt and Hersh, Health Informatics: Practical Guide
ISO 13606 and openEHR, Electronic Health Record Communication and Reference Model
ISO 18308, Requirements for an Electronic Health Record Architecture
outcomes: Describe the content and structure of an electronic health record and distinguish EHRs, EMRs, personal health records and registries.
Analyse clinical workflows and design structured and unstructured documentation that supports care, reporting and billing.
Design data models for patient records with relational schemas, entity-attribute-value models and openEHR archetypes and templates.
Build rule-based clinical decision support and evaluate alerts for accuracy, relevance and alert fatigue.
Evaluate EHR usability with heuristic and task-based methods and propose changes that reduce clinician burden.
Plan the implementation of a record system in a low-resource clinic, including privacy, access control, infrastructure, training and evaluation.

units.title: What an electronic health record holds
topics: The purposes of a medical record: care, communication, continuity, legal record, billing, research
EHR, EMR, personal health record and registry distinguished; the longitudinal record
Record content: demographics, problem list, allergies, medications, encounters, vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, notes
From paper folders to electronic records: the problem-oriented medical record and SOAP notes
The patient folder in a Ghanaian outpatient department and what is lost between visits

units.title: Clinical workflows and documentation
topics: Mapping clinical workflows: outpatient visits, admissions, ward rounds, maternity, laboratory and pharmacy
Structured versus free-text documentation; templates, forms and smart phrases
Computerised provider order entry and results management; closing the loop on orders
Medication management: prescribing, dispensing, administration records
Documentation for insurance: diagnosis coding and NHIS claims generated from the record
Copy-paste, note bloat and documentation quality

units.title: Data models for patient records
topics: Relational schemas for patients, encounters, observations and orders; normalisation and its limits
Entity-attribute-value models for sparse clinical data; querying them efficiently
openEHR: the two-level model, reference model, archetypes and templates; ISO 13606
Concept-based models in OpenMRS: concepts, observations and forms
Representing time, versions, amendments and provenance in a legal record
Coding record data with SNOMED CT, ICD and LOINC; exporting to FHIR

units.title: Clinical decision support
topics: Kinds of decision support: alerts, reminders, order sets, dose calculators, guidelines, dashboards
Rule-based systems and the knowledge base; Arden syntax and CDS Hooks in outline
Implementing guidelines: WHO IMCI for childhood illness, malaria test-and-treat, antenatal care schedules
Drug interaction and allergy checking; dose checking for children
Evaluating decision support: sensitivity, override rates, alert fatigue; the five rights of CDS
Machine learning for prediction in the record: promise, bias and validation

units.title: Usability and clinician burden
topics: Usability principles applied to clinical software; cognitive load and interruption
Heuristic evaluation and task-based usability testing with clinicians; the System Usability Scale
Clinician burnout, time spent on documentation and the click burden
Usability-related patient safety incidents and how design prevents them

units.title: Privacy, consent and access control
topics: Confidentiality, privacy and security; patient rights to access and correct their record
Ghana's Data Protection Act 843: lawful processing, sensitive health data, data subject rights, the Data Protection Commission
Access control models: role-based and attribute-based; break-the-glass emergency access
Consent models: opt-in, opt-out, granular consent; sensitive records such as HIV and mental health
Audit trails, monitoring and responding to breaches; encryption at rest and in transit
Secondary use for research and reporting: de-identification and its limits

units.title: Implementing records in low-resource clinics
topics: Choosing a system: open-source versus commercial; OpenMRS, Bahmni and national systems such as Lightwave e-Health
Infrastructure: intermittent power and connectivity, offline-first design, solar power, device choice, local servers versus cloud
Data migration from paper registers, backup and disaster recovery
Change management: training, super-users, champions, workflow redesign, parallel running
Monitoring adoption and evaluating impact on care quality and efficiency
Case studies of EHR rollouts in Ghana, Rwanda, Kenya and Malawi

units.title: Project
topics: Specifying requirements for a chosen clinic and its workflows
Configuring forms, decision rules and access roles in a simulated record system
Usability testing with realistic clinical scenarios
Project: an implementation plan and working prototype record for a rural health centre

schedule.title: Records and their purposes
schedule.exercise: Compare a paper outpatient folder with an electronic record for one patient over three visits, listing what information is lost or hard to find on paper.

tasks.title: Read a paper outpatient folder for a returning patient and list the missing, duplicated or unreadable items that would change today's care
Convert a free-text consultation into a SOAP note and a problem list, and check what each format makes easier for the next clinician
Draw a diagram of how a patient's longitudinal record is assembled across clinic, laboratory and hospital, and mark where data can be lost between visits

schedule.title: Clinical workflows and order entry
schedule.exercise: Map the workflow of a malaria patient from registration to pharmacy on one page, marking each handover and where an error could creep in.

tasks.title: Draw a BPMN workflow for an outpatient visit from registration to pharmacy, with swimlanes for clerk, nurse, doctor, laboratory and pharmacist
Work through an order entry scenario with a lost laboratory result, identify the broken loop, and choose the fix that closes it
Redesign a documentation template for antenatal visits to balance structured fields and free text, tested against a rubric of time and completeness

schedule.title: Medications and documentation quality
schedule.exercise: Review a sample note with copied text and note bloat, mark the errors, and rewrite it in a concise and accurate form.

tasks.title: Trace a prescription from order through dispensing to administration in a ward case and mark each point where a wrong dose could occur
Generate an NHIS claim summary from diagnosis codes in a patient table and find the claims that would be rejected for missing data
Audit ten copied-forward notes in a case file, identify the clinical error each hides, and recommend controls against copy-paste risk

schedule.title: Clinical data models
schedule.exercise: Compare a relational design and an entity-attribute-value design for lab results, listing one query that each makes easy and one that each makes slow.

tasks.title: Create tables for patients, encounters, observations and orders with keys, and insert a week of data for five patients
Store sparse clinical observations in an entity-attribute-value table and write queries that pivot them back into one row per visit
Model a blood pressure archetype with constraints and a template for a clinic visit, and explain how the two-level approach lets models change safely

schedule.title: Concepts, time and coding
schedule.exercise: Explain with an example why a legal record needs amendments and versions rather than overwriting, and design the fields that support it.

tasks.title: Define five concepts and record observations against them in a concept-based schema, then query all values for one concept
Design versioned tables that keep every amendment with author and time, then show a query that rebuilds the record as it stood on a past date
Map ten local diagnosis and lab terms to ICD, SNOMED CT and LOINC codes and export a patient summary as a FHIR-style structure

schedule.title: Clinical decision support
schedule.exercise: Write the logic of a malaria test-and-treat reminder as plain if-then rules, covering the exceptions for pregnancy and young children.

tasks.title: Sort eight example alerts into types of decision support and say which clinician action each is meant to trigger
Encode a rule base for childhood fever from IMCI as database rules and run it against ten test patients to check each output
Implement an antenatal care schedule reminder set, test it on a case file of patients with missed visits, and judge which reminders would be useful

schedule.title: Safety checking and evaluating support
schedule.exercise: Compute sensitivity, override rate and alert burden from a log of 200 alerts, and recommend which rules to retire or tighten.

tasks.title: Write a dose check for a children's paracetamol order using weight, and test it with five patients including one overdose
Analyse an alert log with a high override rate, identify the rules that cause alert fatigue, and justify which to change against the five rights
Review a risk-prediction model case for bias and validation problems on rural data, and decide whether it is safe to deploy, scored with a rubric

schedule.title: Usability and clinician workload
schedule.exercise: Carry out a heuristic review of a screenshot set from a record system, listing at least eight problems with a severity rating for each.

tasks.title: Review a medication ordering screen against usability principles and list five design faults that increase cognitive load
Run a simulated task-based usability test on a record form, time three tasks, count the errors, and compute a System Usability Scale score
Analyse a patient safety incident caused by a confusing screen, find the design root cause, and propose a redesign that would prevent it

schedule.title: Privacy, rights and access control
schedule.exercise: Write a short note explaining what a patient may request under Ghana's data protection law and how the clinic must respond within its record system.

tasks.title: Decide whether five proposed uses of patient data are lawful under the Data Protection Act and give the principle each case relies on
Create role-based access rules for clerk, nurse, doctor and records officer, and test which of them can read, write or amend each table
Handle a break-the-glass emergency access request, then review the audit log and decide whether the access was justified, scored against a rubric

schedule.title: Consent, audit and secondary use
schedule.exercise: Design a consent form and process for sharing HIV records with a referral hospital, stating the choices the patient has and who can see what.

tasks.title: Apply an opt-in and an opt-out consent policy to six patient cases and note where the two give different outcomes
Query an audit table to find which staff viewed one patient record last month and flag the accesses with no care relationship
De-identify a research extract of 500 patients, test re-identification risk with rare combinations of age, village and diagnosis, and report the residual risk

schedule.title: Choosing and deploying systems
schedule.exercise: Prepare a comparison table of two record systems for a rural clinic covering cost, hardware, offline use, support and data ownership.

tasks.title: Compare an open-source and a commercial record system for a district hospital using a weighted scoring sheet and recommend one
Plan the infrastructure for a clinic with unreliable power and internet, choosing devices, solar capacity, local server and backup, within a budget
Migrate 300 paper register entries into a record database, find and fix the duplicates and bad dates, and report the data quality before and after

schedule.title: Change management and rollout lessons
schedule.exercise: Write a training and super-user plan for a new record system in a clinic of twelve staff, with a four-week parallel running schedule.

tasks.title: List the training, workflow and role changes needed for a ward going live, and sequence them across the first month
Compute adoption and consultation-time measures from a usage table before and after rollout, and judge whether care quality improved
Compare rollout case studies from Ghana, Rwanda and Kenya, identify why one failed, and recommend changes to the failed plan

schedule.title: Project: a record system for a rural health centre
schedule.exercise: Project deliverable: submit requirements, an implementation plan and a working prototype record, with usability test results and a short privacy statement.

tasks.title: Interview a simulated health centre nurse and write ten requirements for the record system, ranked by importance to patient care
Configure registration and consultation forms, three decision rules and four access roles in the simulated record system and test each one
Run usability tests of your prototype on three realistic clinical scenarios, score the results, and revise the design to fix the top three problems
